_comment: Committed quality floor, keyed by eval target (see jmi_evals.targets). CI fails below these. Inner keys are either a report-level attribute (accuracy, macro_f1, ...) or '<class>.<metric>'. Per-class entries are skipped when that class has no support in the labelled set, so a file can be tightened as the golden set grows. Raise these only with a commit that shows the measured improvement; lowering one is a deliberate, reviewable act.

english._comment: Deliberately empty, and not a placeholder. The question this target asks — can someone who doesn't speak the local language do this job? — is answered for the app by the deterministic detected_language signal, at 100% coverage instead of the share the LLM quota has reached, so the app filters on that and not on the model's read (ADR 0010). Hand-labelling 200 postings to gate a field nothing filters by would buy a number, not a better tool. An empty floor means CI reports and does not gate, which is honest; a number invented before any measurement would be a guess wearing a threshold's clothes.

visa._comment: Retired, not deleted. The corpus turned out to hold 1 explicit_yes in 730 enriched postings, so explicit_yes.precision is unscoreable rather than unmet (ADR 0007). The floor that was once asserted is recorded under _retired_floor where it documents history instead of gating a build: leaving the numbers as live keys would have made `make evals TARGET=visa` fail on a metric nobody intends to meet again.
